historical_claims.anchor: A bicategory retains the levels of objects, one-cells, and two-cells but weakens the associativity and unit requirements for one-cell composition.
historical_claims.source_locator: Referenced work, formal formulation and context

historical_claims.anchor: In many two-dimensional settings a coherence theorem says that every bicategory is biequivalent to some strict 2-category.
historical_claims.source_locator: Referenced work, formal formulation and context

description: Builds strict 2-categories from functors and natural transformations with vertical and horizontal composition and interchange. Spans and profunctors motivate bicategorical associators, unitors, pentagon and triangle coherence; monoidal categories and biequivalence illustrate strictification before introducing higher-dimensional comparisons.
